description:
**Chief can hit a usage limit, wait for it, resume from it, and report none of it afterwards.**

The data already exists. Every run writes an append-only NDJSON event log (`chief events -l` lists the logs on this host), and two documented blocks ride on it: `usage` on `agent.turn` (`input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cost_usd`, `duration_ms`, `turns`, `model`) and `limit` on the rate-limit events (`hit`, `retry_at`, `waits`, `max_waits`). Nothing reads them back. The command surface — approve · events · gen · init · lint · list · logs · models · monitor · pause · ps · quality · reap · run · update — has no `usage`.

**Deliberately NOT dependent on `104`.** The most useful number here does not need token counts at all. On a subscription plan the question is not *what did this cost* but *how close am I to the five-hour or weekly window* — and **no provider CLI exposes that**: `claude` has no usage subcommand (`--max-budget-usd` is a spend cap, not a report), `devin` has only `auth status`, `codex` has nothing. Only `opencode stats` reports usage at all. So chief's own **rate-limit incident history — how often a limit was hit, how long was lost waiting, when the window reset — is the best signal available on this machine**, and it works for every provider today. `104` makes the dollar half real; this is useful before it lands.

**Aggregation belongs to chief-cloud, and this must not become a second ledger.** `docs/reference/events.md` is explicit: *"chief does not persist, aggregate, or bill anything itself."* This command READS logs chief already wrote and prints a report. It stores nothing new, bills nothing, and adds no daemon. If it starts wanting a database, it has gone out of scope.

Align the CLI shape with `97-tasklist-state-report`'s `chief status` where they overlap (`--json`, reporting across repos from a parent directory) so the two read as one tool.

userStories.title: `chief usage` reports spend and limit incidents from the event logs
userStories.description: Read the NDJSON chief already writes. Aggregate per run, and total.
acceptanceCriteria: `chief usage` summarises the logs on this host: turns, tokens and cost where present, per run and in total.
It reports rate-limit incidents — how many times a limit was hit, total time spent waiting, and the last observed reset ETA.
A provider that printed no usage figures reports its turns and its limit incidents with the cost columns EMPTY, never zero — zero is a measurement, empty is an absence.
It reads only existing logs: no new state file, no daemon, no provider call.
It runs correctly when no logs exist yet, saying so rather than failing.
userStories.notes: bash -n bin/chief, test/usage.sh, and test/events.sh: green; fixture report observed 2 turns, 10 input/5 output/15 total tokens, $0.25 cost, 1 limit incident, 60 seconds waiting, and reset ETA 180; no-log case exited 0 with a helpful message

userStories.title: Scoping and a machine feed
userStories.description: Useful interactively and to a script, with the same shape `chief status` uses.
acceptanceCriteria: A time window can be selected (for example the last N days), because a limit window is the unit that matters.
Output can be scoped to one repo, and run from a parent directory to cover every repo beneath it.
`--json` emits a machine-readable form, and its shape is documented.
The human output stays readable when a provider contributes no cost data — the table does not collapse into blank columns.
userStories.notes: bash -n bin/chief + test/usage.sh + test/events.sh: green; --json no-log feed parsed successfully with null unavailable measurements; --days, --repo/--scope filtering and fixed-width human columns implemented and documented in docs/reference/usage.md

userStories.title: Wired into the roster the way every other command is
userStories.description: Chief's own providers guide is emphatic that roster surfaces drift when only some are updated.
acceptanceCriteria: `chief usage --help` and the `chief help` usage block both document it.
The README command table gains a row — `test/doc-sync.sh` fails without it.
A test covering the aggregation is registered in `test/all.sh`'s `BASH_SUITE` and given its own CI step, because CI enumerates the shell tests individually rather than running `all.sh`.
The test drives real fixture logs, including a log with null usage and a log with rate-limit events, and asserts the reported figures.
`VERSION` is bumped and the README version string synced.
userStories.notes: bash -n + test/usage-report.sh + test/usage.sh + test/events.sh + test/doc-sync.sh + test/version-bump.sh: green; fixture report observed 2 runs, 3 turns, 10/5/15 tokens, $0.25 cost, 1 limit incident, 60 seconds waiting, and a non-null reset ETA while preserving null usage; README/help, all.sh, CI, and VERSION 0.8.80 synced
